fatal_errors: The cited W study concerns an AlCoCrFeNiWx coating evaluated at 800 °C, not a bulk, initially single-phase CoCrFeNi alloy across room temperature to 800 °C; it cannot support the claimed full-range performance.
The proposed oxide-mediated adaptive film is asserted to function in vacuum or inert conditions, where the oxidation needed to generate that film would be strongly suppressed.
No cited evidence supports formation of a continuous low-shear W-rich tribofilm from only 0.5 at.% W, particularly at room and intermediate temperatures.
The intervention omits the target composite architecture containing Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3 and does not reconstruct the investigated variation in Mo content.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective and offers a single, testable alloying intervention, but it is neither a reconstruction of the target study nor adequately supported as a wide-temperature alternative. It substitutes dilute W alloying into nominally unmodified CoCrFeNi for Mo variation in a multi-component self-lubricating composite. Its lattice-distortion and hard-particle arguments have limited analogy to the target mechanism, but it misses the temperature-dependent division between MoS2/Ag lubrication at low-to-medium temperature and oxide/silver-molybdate glaze formation at high temperature. The baseline is generic and incorrectly assumes monotonically worsening high-temperature behavior. Loads, speeds, and sliding distance are left unspecified, so the claimed operating envelope is not defined. The paired control experiment is directionally sound and includes friction, wear, and microscopy, but it needs fixed test conditions, replication, statistical criteria, and chemical identification of the proposed film. E2 provides only narrow evidence for W-enhanced wear resistance in a different Al-containing coating at 800 °C; E1 and E3 do not substantiate the proposed tribological mechanism or full-range outcome. Consequently, claims of coefficient of friction below 0.2–0.3 and order-of-magnitude wear reduction across all temperatures, loads, and both air and vacuum are unsupported extrapolations.
